**Last checked:** 2026-11-07, against `phase1/planar` at `b551f5b` in
`Symplectomorphism/c-gnn`. The full records are in the discussion
compendium (`reports/discussion-compendium/`); commits are on that branch.

## Open

[]{#step3-choices}

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## Step-3 choices await review: solver, cost, ε<sub>pen</sub>, transition pose, sweep
1. **The solver.** MPPI does not realize the pivot or break(g<sub>v</sub>)
   (next entry). Recommended: keep cost E and change the realizer for the
   edits that hold the box on a corner (contact-implicit MPC or a contact
   trust region); a cheaper first test is a longer look-ahead and more
   samples on the pivot alone.
2. **The cost.** Recommended: **E**, the paper's terms over ε<sub>on</sub>
   (best overlap and follow-on rate, ties B on successes). MPPI's default is
   still A, which overlaps up to 14 mm.
3. **ε<sub>pen</sub>.** Recommended: **5 mm**: covers E's deepest overlap
   (4.7 mm) and cuts ties from 475 to 257 of 4,000. The scene still uses
   10 mm.
4. **The transition pose and thresholds.** The gate accepts at margin ≥ 0
   (float32 boundary acceptances are therefore not removed). The pose handed
   to the solver is the nearest grid pose with margin ≥ 0.02 (provisional);
   recommended: the nearest with margin ≥ 0.1.
5. **The sweep.** Recommended: keep 5 points per direction and range 0.05 for
   now; the sweep uses at most three free directions, so formations with
   more (e.g. {m<sub>x</sub>} with box and disk free) get a slice. Revisit
   with the scene families.

[The local solver](local-solver.qmd), [the hold gate](hold-gate.qmd#sweep).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## MPPI does not realize the pivot or break(g<sub>v</sub>) (checkpoint 2)
Under all five costs, 0 of 3 starts each; the best costs realize 12 of 25
edits that pass the gate. The search cannot follow the chain past the
pivot. Fix: change the solver for these edits (choice 1 above).
[The local solver](local-solver.qmd).
:::

[]{#eps-pen}

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Ties under deep overlap (ε<sub>pen</sub> = 10 mm is provisional)
ε<sub>pen</sub> is ten times ε<sub>on</sub>, so both corners of a tilted box
edge can count as touching. 475 of 4,000 demo poses jittered by about 3 mm
are ambiguous (474 with a contact deeper than ε<sub>on</sub>; in 136,
s<sub>v</sub> loses to t, which contains it). A tied pose is never a search
node or a solver success, so no wrong label is used; the stress test's
budget is 500. Fix: the ε<sub>pen</sub> choice (step 3; 257 ties at 5 mm, 44
at 2 mm). [Contact states](contact-states.qmd#the-recognizer).
:::

[]{#validity}

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Validity is a pairwise stand-in until step 4
A formation should be valid exactly when some admissible pose realizes it
(decided Nov 7, compendium Decision 11). Today validity uses derived
exclusions plus four declared pairs, which admits formations no pose
realizes, e.g. the box bottom on floor and platform at once. The pivot's
compound status rests on the declared pairs {g<sub>v</sub>, s} and
{g, s<sub>v</sub>}, and some of its 64 contexts are impossible. Fix:
validity computed from the geometry per formation, with the scene families
(step 4). [Edits](edits.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## The search: success flag ignored, requested formation stored, breaks unchecked, no goal
Angelo's `Search` accepts when the requested contacts are in band, ignoring
the solver's success flag; a node stores the requested formation, not the
one reached (28 of 30 nodes in a 12-round run); a break is accepted without
checking that the contact left (6 of 7); there is no goal test, goal input
or budget. Fix: wiring Λ's shared success test into the search, then the
goal-directed search of step 4. Walkthrough [8](../code-walkthrough/08-search.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## The hold tests are float32
The gate agrees with a float64 reference on 1,000 of 1,000 random cases and
on every near-boundary case 0.33 mm or more from the boundary. Its only
misses are acceptances with margin 0 (at most 2·10<sup>−7</sup>) at the
boundary pose itself. A positive acceptance threshold would refuse them
(choice 4 above). [The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd#accuracy).
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## The LP gate in 3D needs reinversion
Float32 rounding builds up in linrax's dense tableau over the long pivot
sequences of 3D cones: about 1% of supported 3D cases end "uncertain"
(rejected, never certified wrongly). On the GPU the 3D test sees 4
uncertain of 64 against its budget of 2, so
`test_3d_cones_finish_and_never_mislead` fails there; it passes on the
CPU. Fix: rebuild the tableau from the final basis and continue, with the
3D build. [Background](support-tutorial.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Smaller open items
- **Label flicker near θ<sub>e</sub>** along a trajectory (frames 623–625 of
  the demo). Fix: hysteresis with thresholds from a noise model, in the
  execution monitor.
- **GPU runs are not repeatable between processes** by default (one MPPI
  call ended flush once and tipped 1.4° once). Workaround:
  `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true`, about 13% slower.
- **The 3D catalog** (`step.yaml`) keeps the old defects (closed faces
  over-count, ±y faces, a Python loop over templates). Frozen with 3D.
- **`ContactGraph` drops edges** (`self.edges` never set). Nothing uses the
  graph; superseded by attention over templates.
- **`tests/test_local_solver.py`** reads `gradient_warm_start`, which MPPI no
  longer has. For a fix-up PR to Angelo.
- **The paper's pending results:** step-3 choices and results, the scene
  families and the ranker are marked *pending* in the rewritten paper.
:::

## Resolved

[]{#decision-9}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Xiao and Ji's construction adopted (Nov 7, `9261ece`)
Our construction had drifted from Xiao and Ji's contact formations in ways
that were conveniences, not needs. A literature search (13 papers read in
full) found nothing simpler that still meets our needs: stances,
body-pair strata and scene graphs cannot see a box tip from its edge onto
its corner; configuration-space cells and triangulated subcontacts split one
motion into several edges. We now follow Xiao and Ji exactly and add only
tolerances, several bodies with a manipulator, and a no-contact state per
pair.

| | Before (`84827c0`) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Environment | three convex bodies; the step corner owned by the riser | one polygon E; convex vertices from the geometry |
| Contacts per pair | at most one per body pair | at most one per pair of convex elements, none alongside one it contains |
| Transfers | same or adjacent features: 92 pairs, only 48 Xiao–Ji neighbors | one-sided containment: 56 pairs |
| Compound edges | two transfers in different body pairs | all relaxing or all constraining, every proper subset invalid (same 128 on the step) |
| Valid formations | 11,959 of 12,393 | 37,203 of 59,049 |

The landed box became {t} (next entry). [Contact states](contact-states.qmd), [edits](edits.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The landed box is {t}, not {s<sub>v</sub>, t} (Nov 7, accepted by Aykut)
Once +x<sub>B</sub> lies on the platform, v<sub>S</sub> bounds the touching
platform edge, so s<sub>v</sub> is not principal. Landing is
transfer(s<sub>v</sub> → t), sliding off the corner is transport, and the
chain is one edit shorter. Support is unchanged. [Edits](edits.qmd#the-step-chain).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Transfers, the disk around a corner, corner ownership (Nov 7, `9261ece`)
- 44 of the 92 old transfers were not Xiao–Ji neighbors: 20 went round a
  corner in one step, 24 changed both features at once. Transfers are now
  one-sided containment only (56).
- The disk goes round a box corner in two transfers, through its contact
  with the vertex.
- No ownership rule is needed: the environment is one object whose convex
  vertices come from its geometry (this replaces the Nov 5 rule that the
  riser owns the step corner).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Compound edges: the two-transfer rule, then the general rule (Nov 7, `5b25385`, `9261ece`)
The pivot needs g → g<sub>v</sub> and s → s<sub>v</sub> together, since both
one-at-a-time intermediates are excluded. Settled first as a closed form
(two transfers in different body pairs with crossed exclusions), it was
replaced the same day by Xiao and Ji's neighbor relation with the minimality
rule, which gives the same edges on the step and needs no special case.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The gate tests the less-constrained end; a transfer keeps the old normal (Nov 7, `a3789d7`, `9261ece`)
H first tested the contacts that persist through an edit, with the old
contact's normal for a transfer (on the demo the two normals differ by at
most 1.77° where it matters; using the new one changes none of 1,155
decisions). Under Xiao and Ji's containment both follow from one rule: test
the edit's less-constrained end, as multi-contact planners do (Hauser et
al. 2005, 2008; Escande et al. 2013); the normal comes from the feature that
stays.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The margin and the gate's solver (Nov 7, `228950f`)
The margin is set inclusion of a disturbance polytope, by default the ℓ₁
ball (0.2 = μ on the flat box). The disk's force is bounded by its motors
(±1 N, read from the MuJoCo model), which also made margins with the disk
finite; before, its unbounded push made the support cone fill all of 3D.
The LP backbone is the gate; the exact cone test is its cross-check.
[The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The gate at χ₀ refused realizable edits (Nov 7, `41b5721`, `26c96d0`)
break(g<sub>v</sub>) was refused at 30° although tilting further and then
lifting is possible. H now searches near χ₀ over the more-constrained end's
contacts for a transition pose where the less-constrained end holds, and
passes it to the solver. Pose distances use the paper's weight a/2 on
angles. [The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd#sweep).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## One success test for every realizer (Nov 7, `41b5721`)
MPPI graded itself with its own gap-band test. Every realizer now uses the
paper's success test, extended to transfers and compound edges.
[The local solver](local-solver.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The paper rewritten on the current construction (Nov 7, `e2f705c` to `63de648`)
The old draft (archived, tag `paper-v1-2026-11-07`) described corner
ownership, one contact per body pair, the old chain and stale numbers for
h = a/4. The paper was rewritten from scratch and revised after four
independent reviews; the proofs that the gate never refuses a realizable
edit and that the recognizer is correct are in its appendices.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The hold LPs in float32 with linrax (Nov 6, `e29d96f`, `b354251`)
- linrax had no iteration cap and could cycle on degenerate 3D LPs, hanging
  a whole `vmap` batch: its pivot loop is replaced (300 pivots per phase,
  Bland's leaving rule, artificial rows marked correctly).
- It returned infeasible points as optimal in float32: fixed by
  Householder-spread rows, primal and dual from the final basis, pivot
  tolerance 10<sup>−4</sup>, exit cap 10, and every answer checked.
- linrax has no license file; accepted (Aykut, Nov 6), pinned to 0.3.0.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Step 2's foundations (Nov 5, `d810e32`, `1986c73`)
- `Cand` had no validity check (a second contact per pair, excluded
  formations, transport always legal): edits now pass validity, transfer and
  compound rules; transport only when supported.
- No transfer generator: g → g<sub>v</sub> needed a break and a make through
  a formation where the box does not touch the floor.
- MPAX's "not supported" was uncertified (192–194 of 416 supported
  near-boundary cases rejected): replaced by the exact cone test with
  witness and certificate, later by the LP gate.
- The cone test's margin was positive on a single-ray cone and failed below
  three generators: fixed, and the margin proved to be the signed distance.
- JAX's reduced-precision (TF32) GPU products broke the supporting-plane
  checks: dot products are formed elementwise.
- Tied poses are treated as ambiguous: never a node or a solver success.
:::

[]{#theta-e}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The edge-contact tilt θ<sub>e</sub> (Nov 5, `5f5a2e8`)
A length rule ("flat if 7.8 mm lie within 1 mm") called a box tipped 7.35°
flat, and as the box tipped over the step corner it switched the floor
contact at 7.35° but the riser contact at 8.44°, labeling the impossible
{g<sub>v</sub>, s} in between. An angle shared by both contacts fixes this.
Two principled options were compared: the engines' point rule (both ends of
the overlap within 1 mm), which switches floor and riser at 0.46° and 1.83°
and realizes {g<sub>v</sub>, s} on 13 demo frames; and one derived angle,
θ<sub>e</sub> = arcsin(ε<sub>on</sub>/h) ≈ 1.83°, which switches both together
and is exactly the point rule on the riser. The derived angle was adopted
(a 2° value tuned to the demo, `62782b8`, was withdrawn). Hysteresis for
trajectory labels was deferred to the execution monitor.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Step 1's foundations (Nov 4–5, `ca4123b`, `b2665cb`, `583810b`)
- One physical contact lit 3 to 6 template bits (closed features share
  boundaries): replaced by the principal-contact recognizer.
- The hold test used one tie-broken point per contact, blended by
  smoothing, and ±y faces on a planar body: replaced by the contact sets'
  endpoints in a planar catalog.
- Exclusions were integer indices, then dropped; there were no vertex
  features for g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>: named templates and vertices in
  `step2d.yaml`.
- Overlaps were charged to the wrong surface (−31 mm into the platform):
  each overlap is charged to the nearest environment segment or endpoint
  (approved Nov 5).
- A Python loop over templates: one `vmap` per kernel (the 3D catalog still
  loops).
- NaN gradients in the planar kernels: safe norms and roots.
- The tie-break was kept as the recognizer's fallback, with every use
  counted.
- `pyproject.toml` was invalid TOML: fixed upstream.
:::
